title: The Roots of International Perceptions: Simulating US Attitude Changes Towards China with LLM Agents

bias_targets.methodology: Simulating a representative agent population of US citizens over a 20-year period to measure the evolution of their favorable or unfavorable attitudes toward China based on news consumption, and comparing the simulated opinion valences against real-world longitudinal survey data from Pew Research and Gallup.

Implementing a 'debiasing' intervention where an LLM agent rewrites news articles to remove subjective framing, emotional language, and sensationalism, and comparing the resulting agent attitude trajectories against those of agents exposed to the original, biased media texts.

Conducting ablation studies (e.g., 'No Selection') that remove the agents' ability to selectively choose which news articles to read based on headlines, evaluating how selective exposure and confirmation bias affect the speed and severity of negative opinion formation.
